```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(GenVarJSON)
```

# Overview

Nirvana and Illumina Connected Annotations JSON output is line-oriented:
the first line contains the header and opens the position array, each
subsequent position occupies one line, and an optional top-level gene array
follows the position array. `GenVarJSON` uses this organization to avoid
parsing the complete document as one in-memory JSON object.

The package preserves the output structure used by the aPRoVAR
`read_json.R` workflow. It does not join records, normalize variant keys, or
change row order.

# Read the three raw sections

```{r sections}
example_file <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "nirvana-example.json",
    package = "GenVarJSON"
)

resultados_ultra_v2 <- read_nirvana_sections(
    example_file,
    verbose = FALSE
)

names(resultados_ultra_v2)
lengths(resultados_ultra_v2)
```

The result contains one header JSON string, a character vector of position
records, and a character vector of gene records. A file without the
top-level gene section returns `character(0)` for `genes`.

# Parse the records

```{r parse}
header <- parse_nirvana_header(resultados_ultra_v2$header)

positions_list <- parse_nirvana_records(
    resultados_ultra_v2$positions,
    workers = 1L,
    progress = FALSE
)

genes_list <- parse_nirvana_records(
    resultados_ultra_v2$genes,
    workers = 1L,
    progress = FALSE
)
```

For a large local file, set `workers` to the number of independent R
processes that is appropriate for the available memory. The package restores
the previous `future` plan after each parallel call.

# Create the original aPRoVAR tibbles

```{r tibbles}
tbl_inicial <- nirvana_positions_tibble(positions_list)
tbl_genes <- nirvana_genes_tibble(genes_list)

tbl_inicial
tbl_genes
```

Nested objects remain list-columns. In particular, variant-level annotation
databases such as `gnomad` and `gnomad-exome` are not combined or discarded.

# Run the complete import

```{r one-call}
result <- read_nirvana_json(
    example_file,
    workers = 1L,
    progress = FALSE,
    verbose = FALSE
)

names(result)
```

# Convert positions to GRanges

```{r granges}
ranges <- nirvana_positions_granges(result$tbl_inicial)
ranges
```

The conversion is an additional representation. It does not modify
`tbl_inicial`.
